Hook: The Blame Pie catches the moment when your mind is making you responsible for more than your share and gives you another route.
Mission: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
Game Move: Begin where it says Imagine A Pie; stop the moment you complete Choose Repair.
How to Play:
🎮 THE BLAME PIE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Repair be enough.
POWER-UP 1: Right before the first move, Imagine A Pie, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
POWER-UP 2: At Check The Whole, separate responsibility from punishment.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Choose Repair, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You reach Choose Repair with a clearer distinction between the reaction and the response.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found my slice. I don't own the whole pie.”
Formula Flow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
Safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.

Ritual Title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
Hook: Try Close One Door For Thirty Seconds when every option feels too important to choose. It creates just enough space for a different response.
Mission: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
Game Move: Start with Close Door. When Choose Next appears, the round is over.
How to Play:
🎮 CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Next. No second lap.
POWER-UP 1: Just before you start Close Door, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
POWER-UP 2: At Reopen Choice, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Choose Next, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
Choose Next becomes possible without giving the reaction another full round.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just found a next choice without solving my whole future.”
Formula Flow: Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
Safety:
PAUSE
Do not use pretend closure for urgent, coercive, unsafe, or irreversible choices.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Hook: When you keep needing one more answer before you can settle, The Control Graveyard gives you something concrete to do with the moment.
Mission: Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.
Game Move: Begin where it says Use Control; stop the moment you complete Choose Experiment.
How to Play:
🎮 THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Use Control — Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, reassurance, overworking.
2. Picture Short — Beside each, Picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus On Costs — Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose Experiment — Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Experiment be enough.
POWER-UP 1: Right before the first move, Use Control, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
POWER-UP 2: At Focus On Costs, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Choose Experiment, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can complete Choose Experiment without needing perfect certainty first.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped asking for one more guarantee.”
Formula Flow: Use Control → Picture Short → Focus On Costs → Choose Experiment
Safety:
PAUSE

Hook: The Third Voice catches the moment when a strong feeling is starting to sound like a fact and gives you another route.
Mission: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.
Game Move: Move through the sequence once, from Open Voices to Use Wisdom.
How to Play:
🎮 THE THIRD VOICE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Open Voices — Complete three lines.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting.

⚡ FINISH — Use Wisdom closes the round.
POWER-UP 1: Before you begin Open Voices, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
POWER-UP 2: At Name Facts, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
POWER-UP 3: When you reach Use Wisdom, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.
Win / Reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You arrive at Use Wisdom with less need to obey the first answer.

📸 MY RESULT
“The feeling was real. It still wasn't the whole evidence.”
Formula Flow: Open Voices → Name Feeling → Name Facts → Build Wisdom → Use Wisdom
Safety:
PAUSE
Delay major action if either witness is too impaired to give usable information.
